item.title: NEET protest: All SOPs followed, pellet gun use on protesters authorised - CRPF review
item.description: CRPF analysis indicates police action against protesters followed standard operating procedures. Non-lethal means like pellet guns were authorized for crowd dispersal. Force gradient was followed, with lower measures failing before pump action guns. Protesters and personnel sustained injuries during the July 20 incident. The matter is now sub judice before the Supreme Court.
item.dc:creator: BHARTI JAIN

item.title: Trump, Netanyahu hold 'excellent' White House meeting as Iran differences come into focus
item.description: US President Trump and Prime Minister Netanyahu met at the White House to discuss Iran. Both leaders sought to manage differences over the future course of the conflict. They also discussed implementing a US-Israel framework agreement with Lebanon. Discussions also covered expanding the Abraham Accords and Gaza stabilization efforts. Both leaders face domestic political challenges and changing regional dynamics.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: After stalemate, government, opposition spar over paper leak law in Lok Sabha
item.description: Parliament debated a bill to strengthen penalties for exam paper leaks. Opposition members supported student protests and criticized police actions during demonstrations. Government speakers highlighted past paper leaks and PM Modi's reform efforts. They emphasized the bill's aim to protect student welfare and ensure fair examinations. The proposed law seeks to deter organized gangs and individuals involved in leaks.
item.dc:creator: KUMAR RAKESH

item.title: CWG 2026: Gulveer Singh creates history, becomes first Indian to win Men's 10,000m medal
item.description: Gulveer Singh secured a historic silver medal in the men's 10,000m race. He became the first Indian to achieve this feat at the Commonwealth Games. Singh finished second behind Australia's Ky Robinson in Glasgow. The national record holder clocked a time of 27:49.78 during the event. This achievement marks a significant milestone for Indian athletics.
item.dc:creator: TOI SPORTS DESK

item.title: What made California's largest AI datacenter file a lawsuit over access to river water
item.description: California's largest AI data centre seeks Colorado River water after wastewater plans failed. The company needs 287 million gallons annually for its proposed facility. Local cities and the Imperial Irrigation District rejected its initial water requests. This move raises concerns about the impact on regional farming and jobs. The data centre promises economic benefits and construction employment opportunities.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Reports on alleged cybersecurity incident involving DRDO are incorrect: Sources
item.description: Official sources have denied reports of a cybersecurity incident involving DRDO data. Investigations found no evidence of active cyber attacks or unauthorized network intrusions. Most alleged leaked data is unclassified and from an old breach. Threat actors fabricated documents to appear recent and confidential for financial gain. The department stated the outdated data has no current relevance.
item.dc:creator: SURENDRA SINGH

item.title: Ahmedabad tragedy: SC accepts pilot dad's plea not to make Air India crash report public
item.description: The Supreme Court accepted a father's request concerning the air crash inquiry report. The government will submit the final report in a sealed cover to the court. An NGO questioned the inquiry's impartiality and adherence to standard procedures. The Air Accident Investigation Bureau anticipates completing its investigation within six weeks. The final report is expected to be ready for distribution around October 2026.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: US man arrested for wiping phone during airport search; Android OS may trouble Europe travellers
item.description: A federal case in Atlanta questions privacy software use as criminal intent evidence. Prosecutors accuse Samuel Tunick of wiping his phone to prevent authorities from accessing its contents. GrapheneOS, a privacy-focused operating system, is central to the ongoing legal proceedings. Authorities in Europe also reportedly view GrapheneOS usage with suspicion. GrapheneOS developers state their software is legal and protects against unauthorized data extraction.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Shipping min Sonowal says no Indian seafarer should be caught in crossfire
item.description: Indian shipping minister directed officials to safeguard seafarers from geopolitical conflicts. The government prioritizes the safety and welfare of Indian mariners serving on merchant vessels. Officials reviewed security situations and diplomatic mission preparedness in conflict zones. A union reported Indian sailors trapped in a Ukrainian port facing drone attacks. Mental health support and pre-departure risk awareness programs were also emphasized.
item.dc:creator: DIPAK K DASH

item.title: Canadian boy’s $10 trash-bin cleaning business gets 40 clients
item.description: A young Canadian entrepreneur, just eleven years old, started a trash-bin cleaning service to earn some pocket money. His venture quickly attracted a large social media following and a multitude of clients, particularly during a tough summer job market for teens. With plans to keep the business growing into the colder months, he stands as an inspiring example for children worldwide to initiate their own entrepreneurial journeys.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: A single tree can make 9 million seeds - and it's invading Queensland
item.description: An ornamental tree planted in Tahiti in 1937 now poses a serious biosecurity threat. This invasive miconia species aggressively invades forests and smothers native vegetation. A single mature tree can produce millions of seeds, rapidly spreading across landscapes. Queensland's World Heritage rainforests face irreversible ecological damage from this plant. Early detection and eradication efforts are crucial to protect these precious ecosystems.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: How Europe's heatwave is proving Americans right about air conditioning
item.description: Europeans are now buying air conditioning units in unprecedented numbers. This trend is driven by record heatwaves and rising health concerns across the continent. Manufacturers report significant sales growth for cooling solutions in several European countries. Previously, air conditioning was viewed as an unnecessary luxury by many Europeans. This cultural shift reflects a growing understanding of cooling as an essential need.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Meet Anahat Singh, the Gen Z star who created history for India with a world squash title
item.description: Anahat Singh became the first Indian to win the World Junior Squash Championship. She chose to defer college, dedicating a year to her sport. This decision reflects her commitment to pursuing athletic excellence and future Olympic aspirations. Her journey highlights the importance of discipline and sacrifice in achieving significant goals. Anahat's success inspires young athletes across India to chase their dreams.
item.dc:creator: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK

item.title: 'It is not FIFA's to sell': UEFA blasts Infantino's $20 billion World Cup plan
item.description: UEFA strongly criticises FIFA's ambitious plan to create a new commercial company. This new entity aims to manage major football tournaments and seek private investment. UEFA declares that football's governing institutions have crossed a dangerous and unacceptable line. The European body questions the transparency and governance of this significant proposal. FIFA defends the plan, stating it will strengthen global football.
item.dc:creator: TOI SPORTS DESK

item.title: Trump, Zelenskyy discuss Patriot production, Russia peace talks at White House
item.description: US President Trump and President Zelenskyy met to discuss Ukraine's defense capabilities. They focused on expanding Patriot missile interceptor production and defense cooperation. The leaders also explored efforts to restart stalled peace talks with Russia. Ukraine's president described the meeting as positive and productive for future support. This visit coincided with Senator Lindsey Graham's funeral and a sanctions push.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Nolan Wells' death probe deepens as witness alleges heavy drinking before tragedy
item.description: A new ABC News report says witnesses told investigators Nolan Wells had been drinking heavily before he disappeared on Horn Island on July 4. However, officials have not determined his cause of death. The official autopsy and toxicology results are still pending, while an independent autopsy listed the death as undetermined pending investigation. Ben Crump and Wells’ family continue to seek full answers.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: Deebo Samuel's free agency heats up as top NFL teams emerge as contenders
item.description: Veteran wide receiver Deebo Samuel remains unsigned as training camps open. The Las Vegas Raiders and Los Angeles Rams are reportedly leading the race. Samuel seeks a team where he can contribute his physical, YAC-heavy style. His market is driven by roster fit and timing rather than concerns. A decision on his next team is expected soon.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes' $1.625M gift creates new hope for Texas children
item.description: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes made a lasting impact off the football field with a $1.625 million partnership through the 15 and the Mahomies Foundation. Announced in October 2023, the initiative supports Boys & Girls Clubs in East Texas, Greater Kansas City and Lubbock, while also funding scholarships for hundreds of children and upgrading Club facilities. Here's how the Kansas City Chiefs star and his wife turned their hometown ties into a long-term commitment to help young people build brighter futures.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: India is second-largest sailor supplier in world
item.description: India now ranks as the world's second-largest supplier of seafaring personnel. This significant achievement is highlighted in the BIMCO-ICS Seafarer Workforce Report 2026. The report indicates India's share of global sailors has doubled over the past five years. Indian officers comprise thirteen point four percent of the world's officer workforce. This growth positions India strongly within the global maritime industry.

item.title: Kangana hits back at CJP's Saurav after his response to her 'generation gutter' remark
item.description: BJP MP and actress Kangana Ranaut has once again targeted the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), this time responding to the outfit's spokesperson Saurav Das after his criticism of her remarks on Gen Z protesters. Kangana's reaction came after Saurav Das criticised her comments against Gen Z protesters, including her description of the younger generation as "Generation Gutter".

item.title: ‘It hurts to remember’: Blind since 14, J&K pellet survivor searches for tomorrow
item.description: Insha Mushtaq lost her sight to pellet guns during 2016 Kashmir unrest. She now pursues education and a government job despite her visual impairment. Recent protests in Delhi have reopened old wounds for her. Pellet guns, introduced as non-lethal, caused hundreds of eye injuries in Kashmir. Her story highlights the lasting impact of these weapons on individuals.
item.dc:creator: NASEER GANAI

item.title: 'I regret it': Mehbooba Mufti claims Jantar Mantar remark a slip of tongue, apologises
item.description: Mehbooba Mufti apologized for her Jantar Mantar remark which appeared to justify force in Kashmir. She claimed the controversial statement was a slip of tongue and a misinterpretation. The PDP president stated that her words were taken out of context by political rivals. Governing NC rejected her apology and clarification, demanding a clear response. The party also asked her to apologize for her alliance with the BJP.

item.title: Asmongold breaks silence after Kaise house video as Tectone fuels online drama
item.description: Kaise shared a video from what appeared to be Zack “Asmongold’s” home, joking that he talks to himself for six hours a day. The clip featured Asmongold discussing Tyler Perry before he responded with a humorous comment saying he was not live. Tectone also joined the conversation, while dating rumors surrounding Asmongold and Kaise continue without confirmation.
item.dc:creator: SUMIT ROY

item.title: Jammu and Kashmir: Army duo hurt in Uri accidental blast
item.description: Two Army jawans sustained injuries from an accidental blast near the Line of Control. The incident occurred in the Kamalkote area of Uri sector on Tuesday. Both injured soldiers were promptly transported to the Army Base Hospital in Badamibagh. Medical officials confirmed that both soldiers are currently in stable condition. There is no immediate threat to the lives of the injured personnel.
item.dc:creator: NASEER GANAI

item.title: Jammu and Kashmir: Bus with Amarnath pilgrims slips into gorge, 39 hurt
item.description: Thirty-nine Amarnath pilgrims were injured when their bus fell into a gorge. The bus skidded off the road in Ganiwan, Ganderbal district, on Tuesday morning. A house broke the fall, preventing a more severe tragedy for the pilgrims. Injured devotees were moved to SKIMS in Soura for medical treatment. Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha assured best possible care and safe return arrangements.
item.dc:creator: NASEER GANAI

item.title: Shobhaa De calls Salman Khan's Sonam Wangchuk post 'cringe', slams stars over CJP row
item.description: Author and columnist Shobhaa De has sparked a fresh debate with her latest column, where she criticised Bollywood's response to the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protests and questioned whether celebrities still understand the mood of India's Gen Z audience. De specifically addressed Salman Khan's social media message to activist Sonam Wangchuk, while also taking aim at comments made by Kangana Ranaut, Hema Malini and Anupam Kher during the youth-led movement.

item.title: Archie Goodburn defies inoperable brain tumor to keep Olympic swimming dream alive
item.description: Archie Goodburn reached his first Commonwealth Games 50-meter breaststroke final despite living with inoperable brain cancer. The Scottish swimmer finished seventh but called the experience unforgettable. Along with chasing success in the pool, he continues to raise awareness about brain cancer, hoping future patients will benefit from better treatments and longer lives.

item.title: Pratika Rawal set for County Cricket debut, joins Warwickshire for One-Day Cup
item.description: Indian batter Pratika Rawal joins Warwickshire Bears for the 2026 season. She will strengthen the team's batting in the Metro Bank One-Day Cup. Rawal returns to cricket after recovering from a knee injury. Warwickshire aims for the tournament's knockout stage with her addition. She expressed excitement for county cricket and playing at Edgbaston.

item.title: How injured Tejaswin put aside heartbreak to help Kushare script CWG history
item.description: Tejaswin Shankar's Commonwealth Games high jump ended due to injury. He then coached Sarvesh Kushare, who won a historic silver medal. Kushare credited Shankar's advice for his improved performance during the competition. Shankar's own medal hopes were dashed before the event truly began. He now aims to compete in the decathlon despite his knee issue.
item.dc:creator: TOI SPORTS DESK

item.title: Can India replace a satellite in days? Vikram-1 opens a bigger space question
item.description: India’s space programme has traditionally been driven almost entirely by Isro. Private companies manufactured components, supplied technology and supported missions, but orbital launches remained the domain of the state. Vikram-1 changed that equation. For the first time, an Indian private company has demonstrated the ability to develop and operate an orbital launch vehicle.

item.title: Quote of the Day by Robert Frost: A reflection on mothers, love & life’s unexpected turns
item.description: Robert Frost remains a celebrated American poet known for his accessible yet profound verse. His poems often use rural imagery to explore deep human themes and choices. Frost's journey to success involved years of struggle before achieving recognition. He won four Pulitzer Prizes and recited at a presidential inauguration. His work continues to influence readers worldwide with its timeless insights.

item.title: Cricket club under fire after 'Clicky Ponting' finger-click cheating claim goes viral
item.description: An amateur cricket match has sparked controversy over alleged umpire deception. A fielder reportedly clicked his fingers to simulate an edge off the bat. This incident has led to a formal investigation by the league officials. Other similar allegations have also surfaced against the same club. The league is now examining the dismissals for deliberate deception.
item.dc:creator: TOI SPORTS DESK

item.title: Maharashtra CM directs withdrawal of FIRs against protesters involved in NEET stir
item.description: Maharashtra's Chief Minister has ordered the withdrawal of cases against protesting students. These cases were registered during recent demonstrations supporting the Cockroach Janta Party. Opposition parties urged the government to formally withdraw these pending legal actions. Advocates warned that these cases could jeopardize students' futures and career prospects. The Home Department will issue the necessary orders for case withdrawal soon.
item.dc:creator: VIJAY V SINGH

item.title: 'Milestone' vs 'Pradhan saved Pradhan Mantri': Centre, oppn clash over anti-paper leak bill
item.description: The Lok Sabha is discussing a proposed amendment to the anti-paper leak law. This legislation aims to strengthen safeguards against examination fraud following the NEET exam leak. Union minister Jitendra Singh introduced the bill, reaffirming government commitment to student welfare. Congress criticized the government's response and the handling of student protests. The opposition also questioned the prioritization of social media over education reforms.

item.title: Roberto Mancini returns to rescue Italy after three straight FIFA World Cup misses
item.description: Roberto Mancini has been appointed Italy's new head coach, tasked with rebuilding the national team. He previously led Italy to European Championship glory in 2021. The team failed to qualify for the last three FIFA World Cups. Claudio Ranieri joins as the federation's new technical director. Mancini faces immediate challenges in the Nations League competition.
